name: Callibaetis Spinner
imitates: A spent Callibaetis mayfly on stillwater; tie it for lake fishing when spinners fall on calm water. Change colors to match other spinners.
recipe: Callibaetis-colored turkey biot, ribbed edge standing up

steps.text: Start the thread two eye lengths behind the eye and lay a base to the bend. Lay three strands of DNA fibers in at the bend, angled down on the near side.
Anchor the fibers, wrap forward over their butts and clip them at the starting point. Pull on the tails to separate them.
Clip the tip off a turkey biot, notch facing up, and tie it in by the cut tip at the bend in front of the tails. Return the thread forward.
Fold the biot up with hackle pliers and wrap it forward in slightly overlapping turns, flat edge leading and the raised edge on the back of each turn.
Tie off the biot at the starting point, clip the excess and wrap a smooth thread base for the wing.
Cut 20-25 DNA fibers and lay them across the hook, centered at the front of the biot body.
Tie them down with three tight wraps, pull the far wing out perpendicular and make three more wraps to lock the wings at a right angle.
Dub the thread with a very thin strand of dubbing and begin wrapping behind the eye up to the wing base.
Wrap the dubbed thread through the wing bases in both directions to cover the tie-down, then dub back and forth to a tapered, slightly egg-shaped thorax.
Bar each wing with a few marks from a fine marker tip.
Whip finish, clip the thread, then pull the wings out to form a more pronounced spread profile.
Pull both wings back parallel to the shank and clip them just beyond the bend.
The finished Callibaetis Spinner, side view.
